tools.name: list_chains
tools.description: List every published BlockReq network with its host, public trial URL, private URL pattern ({API_KEY} placeholder), WSS support, and archive and proof/debug/trace flags.

tools.name: get_chain
tools.description: Get one network's URLs and capability flags, its API reference page, and (for EVM networks) the JSON-RPC methods documented for it.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the BlockReq docs (setup, API keys, endpoints, Request Counting, plans, networks, support). Returns page titles, URLs, Markdown URLs for get_doc_page, and snippets. Chinese queries search the Chinese pages.

tools.name: get_doc_page
tools.description: Read one BlockReq docs page as Markdown. Accepts a https://blockreq.com/docs/... URL (HTML or index.md) or a path such as /docs/getting-started/.

tools.name: get_method_reference
tools.description: Get the documented parameters, result, example, and endpoints of one JSON-RPC method on one EVM network, from BlockReq's OpenRPC document.

tools.name: call_rpc
tools.description: Call one read-only JSON-RPC method on an EVM network. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_chains, get_chain, search_docs, get_doc_page · Private data: list_chains, search_docs, get_method_reference, call_rpc · Public sink: call_rpc.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_chains, get_chain, search_docs, get_doc_page · Private data: list_chains, search_docs, get_method_reference, call_rpc · Public sink: call_rpc

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
